{
  "research_question": "How does the stimulation paradigm (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) affect mouse navigation performance metrics including Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": [
    "Combined",
    "ICMS Only",
    "Dim Visual Only",
    "Bright Visual Only",
    "Sham"
  ],
  "response_variables": [
    "Time-to-Target",
    "Success",
    "Path Efficiency",
    "Average Speed",
    "AD"
  ],
  "descriptive_findings": [
    "The Combined paradigm achieved the highest success rate (0.780) and the fastest mean Time-to-Target (2.56), while the Sham group showed significantly lower success (0.273) and longer times (4.68).",
    "Path Efficiency was highest in the Combined (0.503) and Bright Visual Only (0.504) groups, whereas the Sham group had notably lower efficiency (0.308).",
    "Average Speed was highest in the Combined group (12.83), followed closely by Bright Visual Only (12.68), with the Sham group having the lowest speed (10.74).",
    "Angular Dispersion (AD) was highest in the Combined paradigm (0.399) and lowest in the Sham group (0.236), suggesting less straight or more variable turning behavior in the combined stimulation condition compared to the control.",
    "Dim Visual Only and ICMS Only performed similarly, with success rates around 0.67-0.69 and Time-to-Target around 3.0-3.1, indicating neither visual nor ICMS alone matched the efficacy of the Combined approach."
  ],
  "strongest_group_differences": [
    "The most striking difference is in the Success metric, where the Combined group (0.780) vastly outperforms the Sham group (0.273), a difference of approximately 0.507.",
    "Time-to-Target shows the largest absolute gap between Combined (2.56) and Sham (4.68), a difference of 2.12 seconds, with the combined group finishing roughly 79% faster.",
    "Path Efficiency differs most sharply between Combined (0.502) and Sham (0.308), a gap of 0.194, indicating significantly more direct paths in the combined condition.",
    "Success rates for Dim Visual Only (0.673) and ICMS Only (0.685) are intermediate but clearly separated from both the high-performing Combined group and the low-performing Sham group.",
    "AD is highest in the Combined group (0.399) compared to Sham (0.236), suggesting that the combined stimulation leads to greater angular dispersion (less consistent direction) than the sham condition."
  ],
  "practical_interpretation": "The data strongly suggests that the Combined stimulation paradigm is superior to all other conditions, including Sham, for facilitating mouse navigation. It yields the highest success rates, fastest completion times, and most efficient paths. Interestingly, the Combined group exhibits higher angular dispersion (AD) than the Sham group; since AD represents angular deviation, this may imply that while the mice in the Combined group are faster and more successful, their paths may involve more complex or variable directional adjustments compared to the more constrained or less successful behavior in the Sham group. The individual modalities (ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only) show partial benefits over Sham but do not reach the performance levels of the Combined approach.",
  "limitations": [
    "The analysis relies entirely on aggregated summary statistics (means and SDs) without access to individual mouse trajectories or raw time-series data, preventing assessment of within-group variability distribution shapes or outliers.",
    "The sample sizes are unbalanced across groups (Combined: n=48846 vs. Sham: n=3505), which could influence the robustness of mean comparisons despite the large total N.",
    "Statistical significance testing (e.g., ANOVA, t-tests) cannot be performed directly from the provided summary statistics without assuming specific distributions or calculating effect sizes manually, and p-values are not available.",
    "The interpretation of AD as 'angular dispersion' assumes a specific directional relationship (higher AD = more variable/less straight path) which is consistent with the data ranges but should be validated against the raw trajectory definitions.",
    "No temporal analysis of how performance changes over the course of the experiment is possible due to the static summary nature of the data."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Conduct a one-way ANOVA for each of the five response variables to test for overall group differences, followed by post-hoc pairwise comparisons (e.g., Tukey's HSD) to identify specific differences between paradigms, particularly focusing on the Sham vs. Combined and Sham vs. Individual Modalities contrasts. Additionally, perform a mixed-effects model with 'Mouse' as a random effect to account for inter-individual variability given the small number of mice (8 levels) relative to the large number of trials."
}
